passages.note: Bill details page lists Mishler as a Senate sponsor of HB 1002 (2022), the bill that cut the individual income tax rate and repealed the utility receipts tax.
passages.actor_quote: Sponsored by: Sen. Ryan Mishler, Sen. Travis Holdman, Sen. Lonnie Randolph.

passages.provision_quote: (3) For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2016, and before January 1, 2023, three and twenty-three hundredths percent (3.23%). (4) For taxable years beginning after December 31, 2022, and before January 1, 2025, three and fifteen hundredths percent (3.15%).
passages.note: The enrolled act's operative text cuts the individual adjusted gross income tax rate for every resident and nonresident taxpayer and separately repeals the utility receipts tax outright.
Senate roll call 374 passed HB 1002's conference committee report 50-0 with Mishler among the Yea votes; a unanimous margin cannot carry a chair alone.
passages.actor_quote: Bray Ford Jon Mishler Walker K
passages.tally_quote: Mishler Yea 50 Various tax matters. Nay 0 Conference Committee Report #1 Excused 0 Not Voting 0

rows.reasoning: Mishler was a Senate sponsor of HB 1002 (2022), whose operative text cut the individual adjusted gross income tax rate from 3.23% to 3.15% for every resident and nonresident taxpayer and outright repealed the utility receipts tax, matching 'Cut taxes broadly, including the main rates most people pay' rather than the 'targeted adjustments' of rung 3. The act does not address the size or scope of government services, so it does not reach the further 'shrink what government does' of rung 5.
